# Airbnb.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/airbnb-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/airbnb-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects rental listing data from Airbnb.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Airbnb Listings and Prices (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-airbnb)
- **Code:** [`airbnb.py`](airbnb.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property](results/property.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Airbnb search for finding rental listings from location queries
- Airbnb property listing pages for:
    - listing info: title, description, room type, overview, amenities, images
    - host details and location coordinates
    - pricing, ratings, and review counts
    - guest review data

## Functions

- `scrape_listings(query, check_in=None, check_out=None, adults=1, max_pages=3)` → `List[AirbnbSearchResult]`: scrape Airbnb search results for a location
- `scrape_properties(urls, check_in=None, check_out=None, adults=1)` → `List[AirbnbProperty]`: scrape Airbnb property pages

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`AirbnbSearchResult`**: `id`, `url`, `title?`, `room_type?`, `rating?`, `review_count?`, `price_total?`
- **`AirbnbProperty`**: `url`, `id`, `title?`, `description?`, `room_type?`, `overview?`, `amenities?`, `images?`, `host?`, `coordinates?`, `location?`, `person_capacity?`, `rating?`, `review_count?`, `price_per_night?`, `price_total?`, `reviews?`
- **`AirbnbReview`**: `id`, `reviewer?`, `rating?`, `date?`, `text?`, `response?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`airbnb.py`](airbnb.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Notes

Airbnb can be difficult to scrape because of scraper blocking and heavy JavaScript rendering, so this scraper uses Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker) feature with JavaScript rendering and residential proxies.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/airbnb-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`, `test_property_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
